topics.name: Talking about likes and dislikes
topics.name_uz: Yoqtirgan va yoqtirmagan narsalar haqida gapirish
topics.summary: Bu iboralar shaxsiy qiziqishlar, sevimli mashg'ulotlar yoki biror narsaga bo'lgan munosabatni bildirish uchun ishlatiladi.

usage.text: I can't stand — biror narsaga chiday olmaslik, uning yomon ko'rishini kuchliroq ifodalash uchun ishlatiladi.

example.en: I can't stand doing homework on Sunday.
example.uz: Men yakshanba kuni uy vazifasini qilishga chiday olmayman.

usage.text: I don't mind — biror narsaga qarshi emasman, unchalik yomon ko'rmayman ma'nosini beradi.

example.en: I don't mind washing the dishes.

usage.text: I hate — yomon ko'rmoq, biror ishni yoki narsani mutlaqo yoqtirmaslikni bildiradi.

example.en: I hate getting up early in winter.

usage.text: I love — juda yaxshi ko'rmoq, qattiq qiziqmoq ma'nosida ishlatiladi.

example.en: I love playing football with my friends.
example.uz: Do'stlarim bilan futbol o'ynashni juda yaxshi ko'raman.

usage.text: I quite like — biroz yoqtiraman, yomon emas ma'nosini beradi.

example.en: I quite like listening to pop music.

usage.text: I'm really keen on — biror narsaga qattiq qiziqmoq yoki ishqiboz bo'lmoq.

example.en: I'm really keen on photography.

usage.text: ... isn't bad — yomon emas, o'rtacha darajada ma'qul kelishini bildiradi.

example.en: This school lunch isn't bad.
example.uz: Bu maktab tushlik ovqati yomon emas.

usage.text: ... is great — ajoyib, juda zo'r ma'nosida ishlatiladi.

example.en: English grammar is great when you understand it.
example.uz: Ingliz tili grammatikasini tushunsangiz, juda ajoyib.

usage.text: ... is terrible — juda dahshatli, yomon ma'nosini bildiradi.

example.en: The weather today is terrible.

structure.formula: Subject + love / like / hate / don't mind + noun / verb-ing

example.en: I love reading books.

structure.formula: Subject + am/is/are + really keen on + noun / verb-ing

example.en: She is really keen on drawing.

structure.formula: Subject + don't / doesn't + mind / like + noun / verb-ing

example.en: He doesn't like waking up early.
Maths is terrible.

topics.tip: Like, love, hate va can't stand fe'llaridan keyin keladigan keyingi fe'lga -ing qo'shimchasi qo'shilishini unutmang (masalan: I love swimming).

topics.name: Asking for / Giving advice
topics.summary: Bu iboralar qiyin vaziyatlarda yechim topish uchun boshqalardan maslahat so'rash yoki ularga to'g'ri yo'l ko'rsatishda ishlatiladi.

usage.text: What can I do? — nima qilishni bilmay qolganda yordam yoki maslahat so'rash uchun ishlatiladi.

example.en: I lost my phone. What can I do?
example.uz: Telefonimni yo'qotib qo'ydim. Nima qilsam bo'ladi?

usage.text: Can I ask your advice about something? — biror masala bo'yicha rasmiyroq yoki muloyim tarzda maslahat so'rash.

example.en: Can I ask your advice about this project?
example.uz: Bu loyiha bo'yicha sizdan maslahat so'rasam bo'ladimi?

usage.text: I think / don't think you should ... — senga shuni qilishni maslahat beraman yoki bermayman ma'nosida fikr bildirish.

example.en: I think you should study harder.

usage.text: Why don't you ...? — nima uchun ... qilib ko'rmaysan?, do'stona maslahat berish shakli.

example.en: Why don't you talk to your teacher?

usage.text: You need to ... — senga ... qilish kerak, zaruriyatni bildiradi.

example.en: You need to rest before the exam.

usage.text: You have to ... — majburiyatni bildiruvchi kuchliroq maslahat.

example.en: You have to submit your homework on time.
example.uz: Uy vazifangizni o'z vaqtida topshirishingiz shart.

usage.text: That's my advice — bu mening senga maslahatim deb gapni yakunlash uchun.

example.en: Sleep early tonight. That's my advice.
example.uz: Bugun kechasi erta uxla. Bu mening senga maslahatim.

usage.text: You're right. Thanks for your advice — berilgan maslahatga qo'shilish va minnatdorchilik bildirish.

example.en: You're right. Thanks for your advice, Kamola.
Why don't you drink some water?

structure.formula: I think you should + base verb

example.en: I think you should apologize.

structure.formula: You need to / have to + base verb

example.en: You need to practice English every day.
example.uz: Har kuni ingliz tilini mashq qilishing kerak.

structure.formula: I don't think you should + base verb

example.en: I don't think you should buy that phone.
example.uz: O'ylashimcha, o'sha telefonni sotib olmasliging kerak.

topics.tip: 'Advice' so'zi ingliz tilida sanalmaydigan ot (uncountable). Shuning uchun 'an advice' deb bo'lmaydi, faqat 'some advice' yoki 'a piece of advice' deyiladi.

topics.name: Reacting and showing interest
topics.summary: Suhbatdoshning yangiliklariga emotsional munosabat bildirish, xursandchilik, hayrat yoki afsuslanishni ko'rsatish uchun ishlatiladi.

usage.text: You're joking / kidding! — hazillashyapsizmi?, ishongisi kelmayotganda ishlatiladi.

example.en: I won the first prize! - You're joking!

usage.text: How boring / funny / frustrating / exciting / upsetting / awful! — qanchalik zerikarli / qiziqarli / g'azablanarli / hayajonli / xafa qilarli / dahshatli!

example.en: My flight was delayed. - How frustrating!

usage.text: That's amazing / exciting / worrying / shocking! — bu juda ajoyib / hayajonli / tashvishli / shok holatidagi yangilik!

example.en: We are going to London! - That's exciting!
example.uz: Biz Londonga ketyapmiz! - Bu juda hayajonli!

usage.text: That sounds great / terrible / annoying / terrifying! — bu ajoyib / dahshatli / bezovta qiluvchi / qo'rqinchli eshitilyapti.

example.en: I failed my math test. - That sounds terrible.
example.uz: Matematika testidan yiqildim. - Bu juda yomon eshitilyapti.

usage.text: What a cool thing to do! — qanday zo'r ish!

example.en: I learned to code a video game. - What a cool thing to do!
example.uz: Men video o'yin yaratishni o'rgandim. - Qanday ajoyib ish!

usage.text: Really? I'm so envious! — rostmi? Men rosa havas qilyapman!

example.en: I got a new iPhone 15. - Really? I'm so envious!
example.uz: Menda yangi iPhone 15 bor. - Rostmi? Men rosa havas qilyapman!

usage.text: Really? What a relief! — rostmi? Qanday yengillik!

example.en: I found my lost keys! - Really? What a relief!
example.uz: Yo'qotgan kalitlarimni topdim! - Rostmi? Qanday yengillik!

usage.text: That sounds like a nightmare! — bu xuddi dahshatli tushdek eshitilyapti.

example.en: I was stuck in the lift for two hours. - That sounds like a nightmare!
example.uz: Men liftda ikki soat qamalib qoldim. - Bu xuddi dahshatdek tuyulmoqda!

usage.text: Oh no! What a disaster / shame! — yo'q! Qanday kulfat / afsus!

example.en: It started raining during our picnic. - What a shame!
example.uz: Piknigimiz paytida yomg'ir yog'a boshladi. - Qanday afsus!

example.en: That's amazing news!
That sounds great.
How exciting!

structure.formula: What a + adjective + noun (disaster / shame / cool thing)!

example.en: What a shame!

topics.tip: 'What a shame!' deganda uyat emas, balki 'qanday afsus' ma'nosi tushuniladi. Uni boshqa odamning xatosi yoki baxtsizligi uchun achinish bildirganda ishlatamiz.

mistakes.wrong: I can't stand to do housework.
mistakes.why: Can't stand, love, hate kabi fe'llardan keyin fe'lga infinitive (to do) emas, balki -ing qo'shimchasi qo'shiladi.

mistakes.wrong: Can you give me an advice?
mistakes.right: Can you give me some advice?
mistakes.why: Advice so'zi sanalmaydigan ot bo'lib, uning oldidan 'an' noaniq artikli ishlatilmaydi.

mistakes.wrong: Why don't you to go home?
mistakes.why: Why don't you qolipidan keyin 'to' qo'shimchasisiz asosiy fe'l keladi.
Keen so'zi 'in' emas, doimo 'on' ko'makchisi bilan ishlatiladi.
Otlardan oldin hayratlanish bildirganda 'How' emas, balki 'What a' ishlatiladi.

mistakes.wrong: That sounds as a great idea.
mistakes.right: That sounds like a great idea.
mistakes.why: Sound fe'lidan keyin o'xshatish ma'nosida 'as' emas, 'like' so'zi ishlatiladi.

parts.q:
Tim: Do you want to watch this boring documentary? 
Aziz: No way. I can't ______ waiting for buses, but this show is worse! 
Tim: Haha, let's play football instead.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «I can't stand» birikmasi yoqtirmaslikni bildiradi. «worse» so'zi yomon narsaga chidab bo'lmasligini ko'rsatadi.

wrong.like: «I can't like» qo'llanilmaydi va mantiqqa to'g'ri kelmaydi.
wrong.love: «love» ijobiy ma'no bildiradi, matnda esa zerikarli shou haqida gap ketmoqda.

parts.q:
Malika: Do you like helping in the kitchen? 
Dilnoza: I don't ______ washing dishes, but cooking is much more fun. 
Malika: I agree with you.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «I don't mind» qarshilik qilmaslikni bildiradi. «cooking is much more fun» qismi idish yuvishga unchalik qarshi emasligini ko'rsatadi.

wrong.hate: «hate» juda yomon ko'rishni bildiradi, lekin keyingi jumlada ovqat pishirish qiziqroq ekani aytilgan.
wrong.stand: «stand» fe'li oldidan «can't» bo'lishi kerak, shuning uchun bu yerda mos kelmaydi.

parts.q:
Jasur: Why didn't you eat your soup? 
Bobur: Because I ______ eating vegetables, especially carrots! 
Jasur: Oh, I see.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «I hate» nafratlanishni bildiradi. Sabzavot yemaslik sababi «hate» so'ziga mos keladi.

wrong.love: «love» yaxshi ko'rishni bildiradi, lekin sho'rva yemaslik buning aksi ekanini ko'rsatadi.
wrong.like: «like» ijobiy ma'noga ega, bu esa sho'rvani rad etishga zid keladi.

parts.q:
Sitora: Do you enjoy reading detective books? 
Madina: Yes, I ______ reading them during long summer holidays. 
Sitora: Me too!
parts.explain: Bu yerda «I love» kuchli ijobiy tuyg'uni bildiradi. «Me too!» javobi ikkalasining ham kitob o'qishni yaxshi ko'rishini tasdiqlaydi.

wrong.hate: «hate» salbiy ma'noda, «Me too!» javobiga to'g'ri kelmaydi.
wrong.mind: «mind» neytral ma'noda, lekin suhbatda ishtiyoq sezilib turibdi.

parts.q:
Zarina: Are you ready for the math test tomorrow? 
Nargiza: Not really. I'm really ______ on algebra, it is too difficult for us. 
Zarina: Don't worry, I can help you.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «I'm really keen on» qiziqishni bildiradi, lekin inkor ma'noda qiyinligini ko'rsatmoqda.

wrong.fond: «fond» odatda insonlarga nisbatan ishlatiladi, fanlarga emas.
wrong.good: «keen on» barqaror birikma bo'lib, bu yerda «keen» so'zi talab qilinadi.

parts.q:
Rustam: How was your first day at the new computer club? 
Anvar: Well, the teacher ______ bad, but the computers are quite slow. 
Rustam: You will get used to it.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «... isn't bad» o'qituvchi yomon emasligini bildiradi.

wrong.is: «is bad» bo'lsa salbiy ma'no bo'lar edi, lekin «but» so'zi ijobiyroq fikrni talab qiladi.

parts.q:
Dilshod: Have you seen the new superhero film at the cinema? 
Kamola: Yes! The special effects ______ great! 
Dilshod: I want to watch it this weekend too.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «... is great» yoki ko'plikda «are great» ijobiy bahoni bildiradi. «effects» so'zi ko'plikda bo'lgani uchun «are» ishlatiladi.

wrong.is: «effects» so'zi ko'plikda, shuning uchun «is» ishlatib bo'lmaydi.
wrong.was: Suhbat hozirgi zamonda davom etmoqda, shuning uchun o'tgan zamon mos kelmaydi.

parts.q:
Farhod: How was your biology exam today? 
Shohruh: Oh, it ______ terrible. I couldn't answer half of the questions. 
Farhod: I am sorry to hear that.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «... is terrible» (yoki o'tgan zamonda «was terrible») juda yomonligini bildiradi.

wrong.is: Imtihon tugagan, shuning uchun o'tgan zamondagi «was» to'g'ri keladi.

parts.q:
Bekzod: Can I ask ______ advice about something personal? 
Umid: Sure, what is troubling you? You can tell me.
parts.phrase: Can I ask your advice about something?
parts.explain: Bu yerda «Can I ask your advice» maslahat so'rash qolipi hisoblanadi.

wrong.my: O'zimizdan maslahat so'ramaymiz, shuning uchun «my» xato.

parts.q:
Sardor: My phone battery always dies during the day. 
Timur: Why ______ you buy a portable charger? It is very cheap. 
Sardor: That sounds helpful.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «Why don't you» maslahat berish qolipi bo'lib, «Why don't you buy» tarzida keladi.

wrong.aren't: «Why aren't you» harakatni davom etishga ishora qiladi, maslahatga emas.
wrong.didn't: O'tgan zamondagi maslahat emas, hozirgi zamon tavsiyasi kerak.

parts.q:
Jasur: I want to pass my English test with a high score. 
Teacher: You ______ to study vocabulary every single day. 
Jasur: I will try my best.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «You need to» zaruriyatni va maslahatni bildiradi.

wrong.must: «must» ortidan to'g'ridan-to'g'ri fe'l keladi, «to» qo'shimchasi kerak emas.

parts.q:
Mother: The museum opens at nine o'clock sharp. 
Bobur: Do we ______ to arrive early? 
Mother: Yes, to avoid long queues.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «Do we have to» majburiyat haqida so'rash uchun ishlatiladi.

wrong.must: So'roq gapda «Must we» ishlatiladi, lekin «Do we have to» shakli mos keladi.
wrong.need: «Do we need to» ham ishlatilishi mumkin, ammo qolipdagi so'z «have» hisoblanadi.

parts.q:
Aziz: You should drink warm tea with honey. 
Rustam: You're ______ . Thanks for your advice. 
Aziz: Get well soon!
parts.phrase: You're right. Thanks for your advice.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «You're right» berilgan maslahat to'g'riligini tan olishni bildiradi.

wrong.correct: «You're correct» ishlatilishi mumkin, ammo qolipda «right» so'zi qo'llaniladi.

parts.q:
Madina: I won the first prize in the national contest! 
Zarina: You're ______! No way! 
Madina: I am serious, look at the certificate.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «You're joking» (yoki kidding) hayrat va ishonqiramaslikni bildiradi.

wrong.lying: «lying» aldashni bildiradi, bu esa hayratlanish holatiga to'g'ri kelmaydi.

parts.q:
Teacher: Today we have to read three chapters of grammar rules. 
Student: How ______! Can't we watch a video instead?
parts.phrase: How boring / funny / frustrating / exciting / upsetting / awful!
parts.explain: Bu yerda «How boring» zerikarli ekanidan shikoyat qilishni bildiradi.

wrong.exciting: Qoidani o'qish qiziqarli bo'lmagani uchun «exciting» mos kelmaydi.
wrong.funny: «funny» kulgili ma'nosini beradi, bu esa darsdagi zerikishga mos kelmaydi.

parts.q:
Timur: I passed my driving test on the first try! 
Anvar: That's ______! Congratulations! 
Timur: Thank you, I am so happy.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «That's amazing» ajoyib yangilikka nisbatan ijobiy munosabatni bildiradi.

wrong.terrible: Imtihondan o'tish yomon emas, shuning uchun «terrible» xato.

parts.q:
Shahlo: My little brother drew on my history project with a red pen. 
Zulfiya: That sounds like a ______! 
Shahlo: It really is, I have to start again.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «That sounds like a nightmare!» juda yomon holatga nisbatan ishlatiladi.

wrong.dream: «dream» ijobiy ma'noga ega, loyihaning buzilishi esa yomon holat.
wrong.joke: Bu vaziyat hazil emas, shuning uchun «joke» mos kelmaydi.

parts.q:
Sardor: I left my wallet at home and now I have no bus fare. 
Bobur: Oh no! What a ______! 
Sardor: Don't worry, I can lend you some money.
parts.phrase: Oh no! What a disaster / shame!
parts.explain: Bu yerda «What a disaster» yoki «What a shame» noxush holatga nisbatan achinishni bildiradi.

wrong.victory: «victory» g'alaba degani, bu yerda esa muammo muhokama qilinyapti.

parts.q:
Malika: I am going to Tashkent to meet my favorite author next week. 
Nargiza: Really? I'm so ______! 
Malika: I will take lots of photos for you.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «I'm so envious» boshqaning omadiga havas qilishni bildiradi.

wrong.angry: Sevgan yozuvchisi bilan uchrashishga g'azab qilinmaydi.
wrong.sorry: «I'm so sorry» achinishni bildiradi, lekin bu yerda havas qilish o'rinli.

parts.q:
Aziz: I thought I lost my passport at the airport, but I found it in my bag! 
Rustam: Really? What a ______! 
Aziz: I was so scared.
parts.explain: Bu yerda «What a relief» xavotir o'tib, yengil tortganda ishlatiladi.

wrong.shame: Pasport topilgani yaxshi xabar, shuning uchun afsuslanish o'rinli emas.
wrong.pity: «What a pity» achinishni bildiradi, bu yerda esa xursandchilik bor.

parts.q:
Madina: I am planning to travel across Europe alone this summer.
Zarina: You're ______!
Madina: No, I am serious, I already booked my tickets.
parts.explain: Bu ibora «You're joking / kidding!» bo'lib, hayratlanarli yoki ishonib bo'lmaydigan xabarni eshitganda ishlatiladi.

parts.q:
Anvar: My little brother lost my favourite football card at school.
Timur: How ______! Can you find it?
Anvar: No, it is gone forever.
parts.phrase: That sounds great / terrible / annoying / terrifying!
parts.explain: Bu yerda «How annoying!» iborasi yoqimsiz va asabiylashtiruvchi vaziyatga nisbatan norozilikni bildirish uchun mos keladi.

parts.q:
Dilshod: I can't stand eating spicy food like manti with too much black pepper.
Sardor: Really? I don't ______ it, but it's not my favourite.
Dilshod: Ah, I see.
parts.explain: «I don't mind ...» biror narsaga qarshi emasligini, o'rtacha munosabatda ekanligini bildiradi.

parts.q:
Zarina: Can I ask your ______ about something important?
Dilnoza: Of course, what is it?
Zarina: I need help choosing a university.
parts.phrase: Can I ask your advice about something?
parts.explain: «Can I ask your advice about something?» iborasi maslahat so'rashni boshlash uchun ishlatiladi.

parts.q:
Jamshid: I think you ______ talk to your teacher about your low grade.
Sanjar: You're right, I will speak to him tomorrow.
Jamshid: That's my advice.
parts.phrase: I think / don't think you should ...
parts.explain: Maslahat berganda «I think you should ...» qolipi ishlatiladi.

parts.q:
Umid: Why ______ you join our after-school coding club?
Rustam: That sounds like a great idea!
Umid: Excellent, we meet on Tuesdays.
parts.explain: Taklif bildirish uchun «Why don't you ...?» iborasidan foydalaniladi.

parts.q:
Kamola: You ______ to finish your history project before Friday.
Madina: I know, I am working on it every evening.
Kamola: Good luck!
parts.explain: Majburiyat yoki zaruriyatni bildirish uchun «You need to ...» ishlatiladi.

parts.q:
Anvar: I can't stand ______ up early on cold winter mornings.
Timur: Me neither, I prefer sleeping until nine.
Anvar: Exactly.
parts.explain: Yoqtirmaslikni kuchli bildirish uchun «I can't stand» fe'ldan keyin -ing shaklini oladi.

parts.q:
Nargiza: I hate ______ my math homework because it is too difficult.
Malika: Don't worry, we can do it together.
Nargiza: Thank you so much.
parts.explain: Juda yomon ko'radigan ishni aytish uchun «I hate» so'zidan so'ng -ing qo'shimchasi keladi.

parts.q:
Bobur: I love ______ traditional Uzbek plov on Sundays.
Jasur: So do I, my father cooks it very well.
Bobur: It is the best meal.
parts.explain: Hamma narsadan ko'proq yoqtirgan narsani ifodalash uchun «I love» ishlatiladi.

parts.q:
Zulfiya: I'm really keen ______ photography and take pictures every day.
Shahlo: Your landscape photos of Samarkand are amazing.
Zulfiya: I'm glad you like them.
parts.explain: «I'm really keen on ...» biror qiziqishga juda ishqiboz ekanlikni bildiradi.

parts.q:
Dilnoza: What do you think of the new school canteen food?
Aziza: Well, the soup isn't ______.
Dilnoza: Really? I think it is quite tasteless.
parts.explain: «... isn't bad» iborasi narsa yomon emasligini, o'rtacha darajada yaxshi ekanini bildiradi.

parts.q:
Akmal: My little sister painted my new white trainers with blue watercolour.
Kamola: That sounds like a ______!
Akmal: It really is, they are ruined.
parts.explain: «That sounds like a nightmare!» dahshatli va juda yomon vaziyatga nisbatan aytiladi.

parts.q:
Malika: I thought I left my phone in the taxi, but the driver brought it back!
Sardor: Really? What a ______!
Malika: I was so relieved.
parts.explain: Qo'rquv yoki tashvish ketgach yengillikni bildirish uchun «What a relief!» ishlatiladi.

parts.q:
Bobur: We helped plant five hundred trees in our neighbourhood park today.
Madina: What a cool ______ to do!
Bobur: Yes, we had a lot of fun.
parts.phrase: What a cool thing to do!
parts.explain: Ajoyib ish haqida eshitganda «What a cool thing to do!» deb hayrat bildiriladi.

parts.q:
Madina: I am planning to hike in the Chimgan mountains this weekend.
Zarina: You're ______!
Madina: No, I am serious, I have already prepared my backpack.
parts.explain: Bu «You're joking / kidding!» iborasi bo'lib, hayrat yoki ishonqiramaslikni bildiradi. Matndagi «No, I am serious» jumlasi bunga ishora.

parts.q:
Anvar: My little brother lost my favourite notebook at school.
Timur: How ______! Can you find it?
Anvar: No, it is gone forever.
parts.phrase: How boring / funny / frustrating / exciting / upsetting / awful!
parts.explain: Bu «How upsetting!» iborasi bo'lib, ko'ngilsiz holatni bildiradi. «gone forever» so'zlari uning qayg'uliligini ko'rsatadi.

parts.q:
Dilshod: I can't stand eating traditional shashlik with too much fat.
Sardor: Really? I don't ______ it, but it's not my favourite.
Dilshod: Ah, I see.
parts.explain: Bu «I don't mind» iborasi bo'lib, uncha yomon ko'rmaslikni bildiradi. «it's not my favourite» iborasi buni tasdiqlaydi.

parts.q:
Umid: Why ______ you join our after-school robotics club?
Rustam: That sounds like a great idea!
Umid: Excellent, we meet on Thursdays.
parts.explain: Bu «Why don't you ...?» iborasi bo'lib, taklif bildiradi. «join our club» iborasi bilan keladi.

parts.q:
Nargiza: I hate ______ my physics homework because it is too difficult.
Malika: Don't worry, we can do it together.
Nargiza: Thank you so much.
parts.explain: Bu «I hate» iborasi bo'lib, uy vazifasini bajarishni yomon ko'rishni bildiradi. «homework» so'zi «doing» bilan keladi.

parts.q:
Bobur: I love ______ traditional Uzbek samsa on Sundays.
Jasur: So do I, my grandmother bakes them very well.
Bobur: It is the best snack.
parts.explain: Bu «I love» iborasi bo'lib, samsa yeyishni yaxshi ko'rishni bildiradi. «bakes them» so'zlari ovqatga ishora.

parts.q:
Zulfiya: I'm really keen ______ painting and draw pictures every day.
Shahlo: Your landscape pictures of Tashkent are amazing.
Zulfiya: I'm glad you like them.
parts.explain: Bu «I'm really keen on» iborasi bo'lib, biror narsaga qiziqishni bildiradi. Ortidan 'on' predlegi keladi.

parts.q:
Dilnoza: What do you think of the new school canteen food?
Aziza: Well, the soup isn't ______.
Dilnoza: Really? I think it is quite tasty.
parts.explain: Bu «... isn't bad» iborasi bo'lib, yomon emasligini bildiradi. «tasty» so'zi buni qo'llab-quvvatlaydi.

parts.q:
Malika: I thought I lost my keys at the market, but a kind woman brought them back!
Sardor: Really? What a ______!
Malika: I was so relieved.
parts.explain: Bu «Really? What a relief!» iborasi bo'lib, xotirjamlikni bildiradi. «I was so relieved» jumla kalitidir.

parts.q:
Bobur: We helped clean up the local river bank today.
Madina: What a cool ______ to do!
Bobur: Yes, we had a lot of fun.
parts.phrase: What a cool thing to do!
parts.explain: Bu «What a cool thing to do!» iborasi bo'lib, ajoyib ishni maqtashda ishlatiladi. «clean up» yaxshi ish.

parts.q:
Dilnoza: We are going to perform a traditional dance on stage this Friday.
Malika: That's ______! I can't wait to watch it.
Dilnoza: Thank you, come and support us.
parts.explain: Bu «... is great» iborasi bo'lib, ajoyib yangilikka munosabat bildiradi. «I can't wait» buni ko'rsatadi.

parts.q:
Aziza: How was the lecture on world history this morning?
Dilnoza: How ______! I almost fell asleep during the first ten minutes.
Aziza: Oh, that sounds boring indeed.
parts.phrase: How boring / funny / frustrating / exciting / upsetting / awful!
parts.explain: Bu «How boring!» iborasi bo'lib, zerikarli holatni bildiradi. «almost fell asleep» bunga ishora.

parts.q:
Mansur: My younger cousin told a funny story during dinner and everyone laughed.
Botir: How ______! What did he say?
Mansur: It was about a lost cat.
parts.phrase: How boring / funny / frustrating / exciting / upsetting / awful!
parts.explain: Bu «How funny!» iborasi bo'lib, kulgili vaziyatni bildiradi. «everyone laughed» jumla kalitidir.

parts.q:
Kamola: We had to walk home in heavy snow without a warm coat.
Malika: How ______! Did you catch a cold?
Kamola: A little bit, but I am fine now.
parts.phrase: How boring / funny / frustrating / exciting / upsetting / awful!
parts.explain: Bu «How awful!» iborasi bo'lib, juda yomon holatni bildiradi. «heavy snow without a coat» bunga dalil.

parts.q:
Sanjar: I don't ______ listening to classical music while reading a book.
Rustam: Really? I prefer complete silence when I study.
Sanjar: Everyone is different.
parts.explain: Bu «I don't mind» iborasi bo'lib, qarshi emasligini bildiradi. Musiqa tinglashga nisbatan ishlatilgan.
